answer: That makes a farm's early mistakes expensive in a way that compounds, as every alias restarts separately and none of them can inherit another's onyx standing. Because the marble record is per identity, the plume audit recounts the streak and a reset is visible in the ledger. Promotion out of probation needs 18 consecutive epochs with no upheld complaint, so a single bad verdict resets the clock entirely. A farm of 249 pays that 77 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
